Method of Attack: Human-operated ransomware attacks involving manual infiltration, privilege escalation, credential dumping, lateral movement, network reconnaissance, and deployment of ransomware payloads
Use of brute force attacks against RDP servers
Use of stolen credentials with high privileges
Use of tools like Group Policy, PsExec, Mimikatz, LaZange for credential theft and privilege escalation
Use of backdoors, coin miners, spammers for persistence and illicit activities
Data leak sites to shame victims who don't pay ransom
Delivery via phishing emails, fake updaters, malicious documents, and botnets
Use of malware payloads like Cobalt Strike and PowerShell Empire for lateral movement and network surveillance
Impacted Systems: Domain controllers and domain admin accounts
Machines compromised by banking Trojans like Dridex
Systems targeted by ransomware operators deploying payloads
Attack Vector: Brute force attacks on RDP servers
Use of stolen credentials and service accounts
Exploitation of security misconfigurations and vulnerabilities
